items.sentence: Resting adult heart rate is usually 60-100 beats per minute in sinus rhythm; irregular with no P waves in atrial fibrillation.
items.note: Search summary: BHF puts a typical adult resting rate at 60-100 bpm and says some people sit outside it; MedlinePlus and AHA agree. 'Sinus rhythm' and the AF half are the unchanged original wording, not re-retrieved.

items.sentence: Chest pain (recorded within 10 minutes of first medical contact when a heart attack is suspected)
items.note: First pass cited QS68; second pass found QS68 has no ECG-timing statement. NHS England North NSTEMI guideline (quoting ESC) recommends a 12-lead ECG within 10 min of first medical contact; AHA/ACC 2021 says within 10 min of arrival (US).

items.sentence: ST elevation in two contiguous leads
items.note: Search summary: Fourth Universal Definition (and fifth, 2026) label STEMI on new ST elevation in two contiguous leads.

items.sentence: A ten-second snapshot: intermittent arrhythmias need longer monitoring, and a normal first ECG does not rule out a heart attack.
items.note: Search summary: NICE CG95 says do not exclude ACS in people with a normal resting 12-lead ECG. The earlier 'a third of heart attacks' figure was not found in any retrieved text (one NSTEMI study gave 16.3%); removed.

items.sentence: Whether a heart attack has occurred when the first tracing is normal (a normal ECG does not exclude one); serial ECGs and troponin are needed
items.note: As above; 'serial ECGs and troponin' is unchanged original wording.
